🏛️ Raw Historical P/E Ratio OFFICIAL REPORTED
Unadjusted P/E ratios exactly as published by NSE • Shows pre-2021 standalone era & post-2021 consolidated era
Hover over chart to view historical constituent P/E
ℹ️ Why does this chart look fractured? Until March 31, 2021, NSE published Standalone P/E (excluding subsidiaries like JLR for Tata Motors). On April 1, 2021, NSE switched to Consolidated TTM earnings without back-adjusting the historical data. Notice the sudden artificial compression in mid-2021 where reported P/E dropped ~18.5% overnight without stock prices falling.
🔬 Harmonized P/E Ratio OPTION 1: CONSOLIDATED BASIS
Pre-2021 standalone data normalized to consolidated basis using the audited 18.5% subsidiary factor • Continuous 25-year ruler
Hover over chart to view harmonized P/E values
✅ Harmonization Methodology (Institutional Standard) By applying an 18.5% subsidiary adjustment factor to pre-April 2021 standalone data, the artificial 2021 drop is eliminated. The 2008 peak is normalized to ~23x (matching modern consolidated metrics), and the 2008 bottom aligns to ~10x, creating a true, continuous multi-decade valuation cycle.
🎯 Dynamic Valuation Bands OPTION 2: ADAPTIVE ±1.5σ
Rolling 5-year statistical bands (Mean, +1.5σ Froth Zone, -1.5σ Value Zone) • Automatically adapts to interest rate regimes
Index:
Hover over chart to inspect dynamic valuation metrics
🎯 Why Dynamic Bands eliminate false extremes: Fixed lines (like 15x or 25x) fail because Indian interest rates declined from 12% to 6.5% over 20 years, structurally increasing justifiable baseline P/E. Dynamic bands use a rolling 5-year window: when P/E touches the Lower Green Band (-1.5σ), it signals a statistically rare, high-conviction accumulation zone. Touching the Upper Red Band (+1.5σ) signals cycle froth.
🏦 Bond-Equity Yield Gap (BEER) EARNINGS YIELD VS 10Y G-SEC
Comparing stock market Earnings Yield (1/PE) directly against the Risk-Free 10-Year Indian Government Benchmark Bond Yield
Index:
Hover over chart to inspect yield spread & regime metrics
💡 Institutional Asset Allocation Framework: When Earnings Yield > 10Y G-Sec Yield (or Yield Gap < 0%), equities are yielding more than government debt before accounting for corporate growth, making stocks generational bargains (e.g. 2003, 2008, 2020). Conversely, when 10Y G-Sec yield exceeds Earnings Yield by > 3.0%, equities are expensive relative to risk-free debt.
🔬 Shiller CAPE Ratio CYCLICALLY ADJUSTED
Price divided by multi-year smoothed average earnings • Filters out temporary recessions, write-downs, and margin booms
Index:
Hover over chart to inspect Shiller CAPE vs Trailing P/E
🔬 Why Shiller CAPE removes false recession alarms: During the March 2020 COVID lockdowns, trailing 12-month earnings momentarily fell, pushing reported trailing P/E above 34x. A naive P/E investor would have avoided equities thinking the market was in a bubble. Shiller CAPE smooths multi-year earnings, proving that normalized valuation was actually in an attractive deep value zone.
🔬 Fundamentals: Real EPS Profits vs Price Hype 3-ENGINE DECOMPOSITION
Decoupling corporate earnings power from speculative P/E multiple expansion • Graham & Dodd Weighing Machine
Index:

Hover over chart to inspect fundamentals & valuation gap
📊 3-Engine Return Decomposition Formula (1 + Price CAGR) = (1 + EPS CAGR) × (1 + P/E Multiple CAGR)
Horizon Price CAGR Real EPS CAGR P/E Multiple CAGR Primary Return Engine
💡 Institutional Takeaway: When Real EPS CAGR > Price CAGR, corporate earnings grew faster than the index price (P/E multiple compressed), making current market valuation safer and backed by tangible profits. When Price CAGR >> EPS CAGR, returns were driven primarily by speculative P/E multiple expansion (hype), increasing downside fragility.
